title: Starter Accelerator Playflow - journal & smoke-test plan
content:
Purpose:
A compact, playbook-style journal for running a 30min->2hr->full-day starter accelerator for new SDK adopters. This is intentionally minimal and operational: smoke tests, fast failure modes, and the exact checkpoints we use during pairing sessions and office-hours.

Audience:
- Developer advocates running live labs
- Devx engineers preparing sample apps
- Solutions engineers doing initial customer handoffs

High-level goals:
- Give a reproducible 30-minute path to a working sample app that calls Redwood hosted inference
- Surface the 2-hour exploration flow (auth, streaming, tools, embeddings)
- Provide a one-day deep-dive checklist (instrumentation, rollout gating, cost profiling)
- Capture common failure modes and recovery commands

Assumptions and prerequisites:
- User has an API key with a sandbox project and <= 5k token quota for testing
- Starter repo cloned: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/starter-accelerator.git
- Local dev tooling: Node 20, Python 3.11 optional, Docker for local stub mode

Quick 30-minute path ("Minimum Delight"):
1) Create sandbox API key (Console -> Projects -> sandbox-onramp)
2) git clone starter repo + cd starter-accelerator/quickstart
3) npm install && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx
4) node ./examples/hello-gen.js  (expect: 1 short generation response)
4a) If generation hangs >5s: check network proxy, then run curl test below.

2-hour exploratory flow (pairing checklist):
- Walk through: auth -> simple gen -> streaming -> function calling -> embeddings -> reranking
- For each step: show console logs, show token/latency breakdown via Console -> Traces -> live (demo account)
- Encourage participants to change prompt and observe token delta
- Guided exercises: integrate an embedding-based semantic search (instructions in /labs/embeddings)

One-day deep-dive (ops + quality):
- Instrumentation: add minimal telemetry hooks (node: sdk.on('request', ...), add custom tags: team, project)
- Cost profiling: use sample 10k prompt set + compare cases: batching=off vs batching=auto
- Rollout gating: create canary route -> send 1% traffic -> monitor latency and regression alerts (alert rule id DEVEXP-879)
- Private deploy quick check: verify VPC peering and KMS access (see /docs/private-checks.md)

Smoke-test scripts and commands (copy-paste):
- Curl simple gen:
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-1-small","input":"Write a two-sentence product description for a whiteboard marker."}'

- Node quick check (examples/hello-gen.js):
  const r = await Redwood.generate({model: 'rwd-1-small', input: 'Hello from the starter flow'});
  console.log(r.output[0].text);

Common failure modes (triage table):
- 401 / invalid key -> check env var, ensure key is sandbox, check project-level IP allowlist
- 502 / connection reset -> likely transient; retry with exponential backoff, check Console -> infra incidents
- Streaming stalls mid-sequence -> verify client network, then toggle streaming=false to confirm behavior
- High latency on long prompts (>2048 tokens) -> suggest quantized variant or reduce seq length, enable prefix caching where possible

Telemetry & observable checkpoints (what to show during a demo):
- Request-level: latency, tokens_in/tokens_out, model_version
- Route-level: P95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens
- Rollout: canary conversion rate, rollback reason (model quality/regression)

Gating criteria for production rollout (minimum):
- P95 latency below SLA target for the route
- No new quality regressions on baseline prompt set (eval pass >= 95%)
- Cost per 1k tokens <= budget target for tier
- Retries and fallback paths validated end-to-end

Teaching tips & nudge points (what gets overlooked):
- Show how prompt edits change token billing in Console; people underestimate prompt framing cost
- Demonstrate how prefix caching yields immediate latency wins for conversational apps
- Encourage small A/B tests on quantization candidates before committing

Sample prompts to drive discussion in lab exercises:
- "Summarize the following text in 3 bullets, prioritize clarity and brevity:"
- "Given a user message, extract intent and 2 entity key-value pairs in JSON."

Open questions / TODOs (parking lot):
- Add a short Python notebook version of the 30-minute flow (tracked: GH #147)
- Better error snippets for enterprise private deploy networking failures (collect examples from eng-private)
- Create a printable one-pager with the 30-minute checklist for AE handoffs

Session logistics (operational notes):
- Ideal class size: 4-6 engineers (pair programming format)
- Timeboxed segments: 30m demo, 60m guided exercises, 30m Q&A/telemetry review
- Environment reset command: ./scripts/reset-lab.sh (wipes local state, regenerates test API key)

Notes to self (Samira):
- Next revision: add a short section on "when to use dedicated vs hosted for early customers" with simple cost rule-of-thumb
- Collect 3 anonymized incident stories where fallback saved a live experiment

Relevant links and references (quick):
- Starter repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/starter-accelerator
- Devx lab board: https://linear.app/redwood/board/DEVX
- Example rollout PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-experience/pull/142

End of journal entry.
